newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SELES WINS FIRST MATCH OF YEAR AT LIPTON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SELES WINS FIRST MATCH OF YEAR AT LIPTON.

text.p: Monica Seles played her first match of the year Friday and survived a three-set challenge in the second round of the Lipton Championships.

Seles, who had been out of action since breaking her finger in December, managed a 6-3 2-6 6-2 victory over Japan's Naoko Sawamatsu on a day in which rain played havoc with the tournament schedule and forced many athletes to wait around for hours to see if they would get their matches in.
Men's top seed Pete Sampras had his scheduled night match put off until Saturday when he will face Romania's Adrian Voinea.

Women's top seed Martina Hingis, who is poised to take the world's top ranking from Steffi Graf at the end of this event, was tested before dispatching unseeded Patricia Hy-Boulais of Canada 3-6 6-3 6-2.
The Swiss teen sensation, who won all four tournaments she has played this year including the Australian Open, ran her 1997 record to a perfect 21-0.
Graf is unable to defend her Lipton title due to a knee injury and will lose her number one ranking to the 16-year-old Hingis on March 31.
"It's a great feeling to be the best tennis player in the world," said Hingis rather immodestly.

"Everybody wants to play me now. Everybody wants to beat me," added Hingis, who struggled with her serve in the first set but raised her game in the second and third to maintain her unblemished 1997 record.
Men's fourth seed Goran Ivanisevic easily beat Byron Black of Zimbabwe 6-3 6-3.
Ivanisevic is looking to return to the final after having had to default three games into last year's final with Andre Agassi due to injury.
Seles, who will lose her record as the youngest ever world number one to Hingis, admitted to being rusty against Sawamatsu.
"My groundstrokes just collapsed on me," Seles said of her middle set lapse. "I need to play quite a few tournaments to get match tough. Today I clearly didn't have that."
After waiting out the rain, Seles was slow to get her strokes going, narrowly winning the first set 6-3.
She dropped her serve twice in losing the second set before assuming control in the third.
"Waiting around all day made me more nervous," Seles said. "But I knew her game."
Seles said her finger was fully healed and she was suffering no pain from the shoulder injury that hampered her play on and off all of last year.
"My finger was broken in two places and all messed up," she said. "It definitely took much longer than I thought. I thought I would be off for six weeks, max."
